The Florida forward scored all three goals in a 3-2 overtime win against the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday. It followed a three-goal, four-point performance in a 7-3 win at the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday. Both were natural hat tricks; the only other players in NHL history to have such a hat trick in consecutive games are Petri Skriko (Nov. 18-21, 1986 with the Canucks) and Cy Denneny (Feb. 21-24, 1923 with the Ottawa Senators). Tkachuk also became the third player in Florida history with a hat trick in consecutive games, joining Noel Acciari (Dec. 16-20, 2019) and Pavel Bure (Feb. 10-14, 2001). The last player in the NHL to have consecutive hat tricks was Toronto Maple Leafs forward Auston Matthews , who score three goals on Feb. 15, 2024, in a 4-3 overtime win against the Philadelphia Flyers and three more (with two assists) two days later in a 9-2 win against the Anaheim Ducks. items.summary: Speaking with the media recently, Red Wings owner Chris Ilitch is prioritizing hiring a President of Hockey Operations instead of a GM right now.
items.body: Register Login Red Wings To Prioritize President Of Hockey Operations Hire By Brian La Rose | at October 16, 2026 10:00 pm Since the Red Wings removed Steve Yzerman from their general manager role, the focus has been on who the new permanent GM will be. After two months, Shawn Horcoff was given the interim title and with Alex DeBrincat ’s seven-year, $91MM extension this week, it’s clear he has the green light to make some moves. But while we’ve been waiting for a lengthy GM search to come to an end, that isn’t going to be the case for the foreseeable future. Speaking with reporters recently including The Athletic’s Max Bultman , team owner Chris Ilitch indicated that his focus is on hiring a President of Hockey Operations. Then, that person can determine if or when a GM will be hired. This follows the approach he took with the Detroit Tigers. Going with a President but not a GM is rather uncommon but there are front offices where the GM is the secondary decision-maker or is making decisions in lockstep with the President. With that in mind, it wouldn’t be shocking if Detroit eventually followed one of those paths and put a GM in place. items.body: Penguins' Sidney Crosby set up Bryan Rust on a two-on-one rush against the Avalanche, recording an assist to move into seventh on the NHL's all-time assists list. Sidney Crosby continues to climb the all-time NHL leaderboards. The Pittsburgh Penguins captain recorded his 1,110th career assist against the Colorado Avalanche on Friday, moving past Joe Thornton for sole possession of seventh place on the NHL’s all-time assists list. Crosby now sits 25 assists behind Paul Coffey, who occupies sixth place with 1,135. Wayne Gretzky remains the league’s all-time leader with 1,963. It’s the latest in a long list of accomplishments for the 39-year-old, who is in his 22nd season with the Penguins and has already established himself as the franchise’s all-time points leader.

items.title: Maple Leafs Place Miles Wood On IR
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs have placed winger Miles Wood on injured reserve.
items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Place Miles Wood On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 16, 2026 8:00 pm The injury list has been pretty long already this season for the Maple Leafs, who find themselves down several regulars in the early going. Now, one of the players called up to cover for those injuries is injured himself without even playing one game. Per the NHL’s media site, winger Miles Wood has been placed on injured reserve. The 31-year-old cleared waivers back in training camp and was assigned to the minors but found himself on the move soon after as he was moved to Toronto as part of the Kirill Marchenko trade. His inclusion appeared to be more for salary cap purposes as he carries a $2.5MM cap charge for the next three years, a hefty price tag for someone to play in the AHL. He earned that money over a decade’s worth of games, where he has 99 goals and 97 assists in 567 appearances. Wood remained on assignment to the Marlies early in the season and hadn’t seen game action prior to his recall last week. He got into some practices and evidently sustained some sort of injury, although the nature is undisclosed and there’s no word on a timeline for his return. Toronto has a little under $5MM remaining in LTIR room, per PuckPedia . That pool will be reduced by $3.25MM in the coming days with Dakota Joshua ’s pending return but even so, they can easily afford to carry Wood on IR for the time being. If Wood is eventually deemed to miss at least 10 games and 24 days, he’ll be eligible to be transferred to LTIR himself. The Maple Leafs now have one open spot on their active roster, though that could be given to Joshua over the next few days.

items.body: Panthers forward 65th player to have consecutive two-goal games entering matchup with Kraken on Saturday Eighty-four times since the NHL’s birth in 1917, a player has scored three or more goals in consecutive games. Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk , the 65th and newest player on the list, is bidding to become the first to make it three in a row -- a hat trick of hat tricks. Tkachuk can make NHL history with three goals on Saturday at Amerant Bank Arena against the visiting Seattle Kraken (6 p.m. ET; Prime Video, SCRIPPS, KONG). The list begins with Cy Denneny , Newsy Lalonde , Joe Malone and Reg Noble in the NHL’s inaugural 1917-18 season. It is capped by Tkachuk, who had three goals and an assist at the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday, then added three goals at home against the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday. Eight times, since Denneny with the Ottawa Senators in 1917 through Teemu Selanne with the Winnipeg Jets in 1993, a player has had consecutive hat tricks and then scored twice in a third game, coming one goal short of the three-peat. Others on the close-but-no-cigar list: Alexander Mogilny , Buffalo Sabres, 1992-93; Wayne Gretzky , Edmonton Oilers, 1984; Phil Esposito , Boston Bruins, 1974; Claude Larose, Montreal Canadiens, 1974; Punch Broadbent , Senators, 1922; and Malone, Hamilton Tigers, 1921. These offensive stars put up gaudy streak numbers, their consecutive hat tricks only part of their stories. Selanne scored nine goals in a three-game span, with fellow rookie Keith Tkachuk , Brady’s father, scoring a goal in all three of those games. Mogilny had 13 goals over five games; Gretzky, nine in three; Esposito, eight in three; Larose, nine in three; Broadbent, 14 in six; Malone, 16 in six; Denneny, 12 in four. items.body: Allowing third-most goals-against in NHL entering game against Rangers Saturday Rick Bowness said everyone associated with the Columbus Blue Jackets "should be very angry with where we are." The coach, speaking on Friday, said he especially was bothered by the fact that the Blue Jackets have allowed an average of 4.20 goals per game, tied for the third most in the NHL. "We're 30th in the League in goals-against -- 30th," Bowness said. "I've never coached a team that was 30th in the League in goals-against." The Blue Jackets (2-3-0), who host the New York Rangers at Nationwide Arena on Saturday (7 p.m. ET; CBJHN, CBJNHL, MSG), haven't played since Tuesday, a 7-3 home loss to the Florida Panthers. That followed a 5-3 loss at the St. Louis Blues on Saturday. They have allowed at least three goals in four of their five games and are 1-3-0 after a 6-3 win against the Buffalo Sabres in their season opener Oct. 1. After the loss to the Panthers, Bowness voiced his frustration with his team. "We beat ourselves in St. Louis. We beat ourselves tonight," Bowness said. "So you have to hope, you've got to believe, that that performance tonight will embarrass them enough to stop this, right? Because if they're not embarrassed by that, we don't want them on the team. It's as simple as that. "I'm not a babysitter. I'm too old to be a babysitter for these guys. You're a professional athlete, prepare yourself to play properly." This is not the first time that Bowness has called out his team. Last season, after the Blue Jackets had been eliminated from Stanley Cup Playoff contention, Bowness said if he returned to Columbus this season, he would be "changing the culture." items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Assign Dakota Joshua On LTIR Conditioning Stint By Brennan McClain | at October 16, 2026 3:30 pm The Toronto Maple Leafs are less than a week away from returning a bottom-six forward. According to the AHL transactions log , the Maple Leafs have assigned Dakota Joshua to the AHL’s Toronto Marlies for a conditioning stint. Per the conditioning loan rules, Joshua can spend up to six days or play in three games with the Marlies, whichever comes first. However, with mutual agreement between Toronto and Joshua, the conditioning stint can be extended for two additional games. Joshua, 30, will begin his second season with the Maple Leafs after being acquired from the Vancouver Canucks ahead of the 2025-26 campaign. He is in the third season of a four-year, $13MM ($3.25MM AAV) contract signed in 2024. Unfortunately, the uber-physical forward has continued his struggles with injuries in Toronto. During the 2023-24 campaign, Joshua missed nearly 20 games due to a hand injury. The following season, Joshua faced a battle with testicular cancer and a severe leg injury, limiting him to 57 games. Last season, his first with the Maple Leafs, Joshua finished with 10 goals and 18 points in 55 games with a -2 rating, averaging 12:15 of ice time per game. items.title: Ducks’ rebuild provides blueprint for Flames to follow
items.summary: As the Flames embark on their own rebuild, the Ducks are beginning to look an awful lot like the blueprint GM Craig Conroy would love to follow, writes Eric Francis.
items.body: That was the timeline Pat Verbeek had in mind shortly after he took the wheel in Anaheim, a franchise that needed to tear things down before it could dream of building something special again. The goal wasn't to win a Stanley Cup in five years. It wasn't even to guarantee a playoff spot. It was to become a team that could start contending for a sprinkling of spring hockey. As the Calgary Flames embark on their own uncomfortable transition, Verbeek's Anaheim Ducks are beginning to look an awful lot like the blueprint Craig Conroy would love to follow. The similarities aren't lost on Verbeek, who has watched his young Ducks take a significant step forward after years of accumulating draft picks, developing talent and carefully adding veterans to help the kids grow. "When I talk to Connie, yeah," Verbeek said of the parallels between Anaheim's rebuild and Calgary's. "Transitioning is probably the hardest thing to do, not wanting to take a step back, but just kind of gaining a little ground every year.” In a one-on-one chat outside the Ducks dressing room, Verbeek said that when he arrived in Anaheim in Feb. 2022, his first instinct was to try to retain the veteran foundation on a team that missed the playoffs three years running. But Josh Manson, Hampus Lindholm and Rickard Rakell couldn't be signed to new deals, forcing the general manager to change course. That pivot, as he calls it, became the foundation of the rebuild. Rather than cling to a group that wasn't going to take the Ducks where they wanted to go, Verbeek traded those veterans and began stockpiling draft picks, putting an emphasis on identifying and developing young talent. According to a team announcement , the Kraken recalled defenseman Ty Nelson from the AHL’s Coachella Valley Firebirds. Seattle had an open roster spot before the transaction, so no corresponding roster move was necessary. Seattle selected Nelson, 22, with the 68th overall pick (third-round) in the 2022 NHL Draft. The Toronto, ON, native played for the OHL’s North Bay Battalion at the time, scoring 40 goals and 128 points in 121 games in his two post-draft campaigns. Nelson has continued his strong two-way play in the AHL. Since debuting with AHL Coachella Valley in 2024-25, he has registered 17 goals and 71 points in 140 games with a +34 rating. He has puck-moving skills similar to those of other smaller defensemen. Still, despite standing at 5’10″and weighing 198 lbs, Nelson plays extremely large. They aren’t all bone-crushing hits, but he plays with an extremely high motor and sacrifices his body almost every shift. Unfortunately, despite his strong play with the Firebirds, Nelson hasn’t made his NHL debut. Depending on the severity of Montour’s injury, that could change during his current recall. items.title: ‘Should all be very angry’: Cooler heads not prevailing for Blue Jackets’ Bowness
items.body: The Columbus Blue Jackets coach continued his public tirade over his team's defence on Friday three days after it suffered a 7-3 loss to the Floridaa Panthers. "Right now, we should all be very angry at where we are," Bowness told reporters . "You look at our team. We’re 30th in the league in goals against. I’ve never coached a team that was 30th in the league in goals against … I’m mad. I keep seeing 30th goals against. That bothers me." Columbus, which sits 3-2 on the season, is tied with the Los Angeles Kings for third-last in the NHL at 4.20 goals against per game. The Blue Jackets fell apart in the second period of the Panthers loss, allowing four goals including a natural hat trick from Brady Tkachuk. Forward Mathieu Olivier did his team no favours either, taking an ill-advised five-minute major penalty for slashing, which led to his subsequent ejection and another goal against. "Yeah. They’re like I am. They’re not happy where they are," he said. The 71-year-old coach ripped into his players in the immediate aftermath of the game on Tuesday, calling the performance "embarrassing." "You gotta believe that performance will embarrass them enough to stop this, right?" Bowness told reporters . "Because if they're not embarrassed by that, we don't want them on the team. Simple as that." "I know it looks bad, but I believe in what we're doing. I believe in them. I believe we can fix the problems," the bench boss added. "That all being said, if (the game) doesn't get their attention, then they're on the wrong team." Blue Jackets players will have their first chance to do just that when they return to the ice Saturday for a home date against the New York Rangers.

items.summary: So Gavin McKenna was benched on Thursday and played less than seven minutes against the Sabres. Justin Bourne takes a detailed look at what the 18-year-old did with his ice time to try and make sense of the benching.
items.body: In the midst of a close divisional game against the Buffalo Sabres, Gavin McKenna found himself stapled to the bench from halfway through the second period through to the final buzzer. He played just 6:36 in total. To my memory, it was one of the longest benchings of a non-fourth line player in years in Toronto, and given it happened to their recent number one overall draft pick, we’re going to talk about it. Raddysh joins the team having played the start of his 2026-27 campaign with three goals for five points in five AHL contests. The former second-round pick is in the second year of a two-year, $1.5MM AAV contract. At age 28, Raddysh has solidified his professional profile as a depth piece for an organization that can provide some worthy second-hand offense. In his first year with New York, he scored 19 points in 68 games. Historically, Raddysh has seen a near 40-point campaign with the Blackhawks back in 2022-23. Even then, penalty killing and defensive prowess are valuable things the Rangers will need out of him, which he has been prominent in. Chmelar, in comparison, has been averaging less NHL time than what Raddysh usually provides in a similar role. The former fifth-round pick out of Czechia has started his first seven NHL games in 2026-27 with around eight minutes of ice time at 5-on-5 and has yet to produce a point. Adam Proteau Partner Oct 16, 2026 2:20 PM Published Oct 16, 2026 2:20 PM The Columbus Blue Jackets are already off to a subpar start to the 2026-27 NHL season. And coach Rick Bowness has already torn into his team. This isn't the first time Bowness has ripped his Jackets players. But are Bowness' outbursts helping or hurting his team? If there’s one thing we know about Rick Bowness, it’s that he does not mince words. The longtime NHL coach has become a media favorite, largely because he doesn’t hesitate to call out his players when they’re not meeting expectations. At 71, Bowness has run out of dams to give, infamously going off on his Columbus Blue Jackets players at the end of another disappointing 2025-26 season. But after a thorough drubbing of the Jackets, 7-3, by the Florida Panthers Tuesday night, Bowness went in on his group again. Needless to say, Columbus’ players are on notice; Bowness isn't getting softer or more cuddly because he’s in a new season with a new collection of players. He built a family in Calgary and experienced the highs and lows of playing in a market where hockey means an awful lot to people. So when he sees his former team struggling through the earliest stages of a rebuild, he understands the frustration. He also knows there's a bigger picture at play. “You never want to see your old team struggle, right?” said the Vegas defender. “But at the same time, they went out and said it's a rebuild, and this is what the fans asked for.” It's a difficult balance for everyone involved. Fans want to see progress, young players need time to develop, and management is trying to build a team capable of competing for years to come. This will take time. Lots of it. Andersson's point isn't that Calgary supporters shouldn't be frustrated. It's that rebuilding is rarely a straight line, and patience becomes particularly important when there are growing pains, like the team’s 1-6 start, arrive. “They can't get impatient,” said Andersson, who has long monitored the pulse of the fans closer than most. “I don't read about it the same way as I did, but it still pops up here and there — I still see some comments like, ‘fire the coach, do this, do this.’ “Did guys think you could win seven in a row to start the season when you guys go out and say you want to rebuild? Thursday’s win also got the Panthers to 10 points on the season, putting them in a three-way tie for second in the Atlantic Division. items.body: More rest, less practice time among potential benefits, Oettinger says Every team in the NHL is required to have an emergency backup goalie on its roster this season as spelled out in the new Collective Bargaining Agreement, but for some, the new job description will go beyond the traditional EBUG duties. Some teams may indeed limit their mandated extra goalie to those in-case-of-emergency-break-glass situations where a last-minute or in-game injury or illness makes it impossible to call up a minor league goalie fast enough to fill in for a game. Other teams plan to use their EBUG to help ease the workload for their regulars in practice too, something that several goalies around the League were looking forward to as soon as the agreement was announced in 2025. Jake Oettinger of the Dallas Stars believes it could even help goalies stay healthier. "I think that having a third goalie, goalie injuries are going to go down a lot because of that," Oettinger told NHL.com during the 2025-26 season. "Having the opportunity to take time when you need it is going to be huge because I feel like half the time, I try to skate as much as I can just because you feel kind of like a (jerk) if you're leaving the boys out there with no goalie. So, that won't be the case where you probably know you shouldn't skate, but you don't want to leave your guys hung out to dry. I think that's going to help a lot." Lund suffered an upper-body injury in a prospect game in September, and it was later announced that he would be sidelined for a month. Standing 6’2″, 195 pounds, Lund had a solid three-year NCAA career at Northeastern University before turning pro late in 2024-25. 2025-26 was Lund’s first full campaign at the pro level, and he scored nine goals and 25 points in 37 AHL games. Lund is generally a well-regarded prospect, although he is not typically counted among the best in what is a deep Sharks farm system. Earlier this year, The Athletic’s Scott Wheeler ranked Lund as the No. 10 prospect in the team’s pool, calling him someone who “has bottom-sixer potential if he can continue to develop.” Now that he’s healthy, Lund will be able to continue building towards that kind of NHL future with the Barracuda. Barre-Boulet is the other player the Sharks reassigned today, and he’s in a very different situation from Lund. The 29-year-old undrafted winger is one of the AHL’s very best point producers, having scored 133 points in his last 134 games at that level. items.body: CHICAGO — Chicago Blackhawks forward Patrick Kane earned another career milestone in becoming the NHL’s career leader in assists among U.S.-born players. The 37-year-old from Buffalo, New York, earned his 895th career assist on Connor Bedard’s game-opening power-play goal against the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday night. In doing so in his 1,377th game, Kane surpassed the American-born record held by defenseman Phil Housley, who had 894 assists in 1,496 games. Kane then added a second assist by having a hand in Artyom Levshunov's goal 1:37 into overtime of a 4-3 win. In January while with the Detroit Red Wings, Kane set the record for most points among American NHLers, with the two assists now increasing his total to 1,405. Kane is in his 20th NHL season and signed a two-year contract in July to return to Chicago where he won three Stanley Cups during his first 16 NHL seasons. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images The Seattle Kraken could be looking at life without their most relied upon blueliner. Kraken defenseman Brandon Montour suffered a lower-body injury during Thursday’s road game against the Tampa Bay Lightning . The team has confirmed that he will not return to the game. It’s not exactly clear how Montour picked up the injury, but it may have occured during his last shift early in the second period when he was tripped up by Lightning forward Nikita Kucherov, causing him to fall somewhat awkwardly. Montour, 32, has no goals and five assists in seven games this season. He is also leading Seattle with a tick over 24 and half minutes of ice time per game. Last season, he notched 11 goals and 21 assists for 32 points in 64 games for Seattle, while leading the team in average ice time with about 22 and a half minutes. The Brantford, Ontario native is in his third season with the Kraken after signing with them on a seven-year, $50 million deal as an unrestricted free agent in July of 2024. Selected by the Anaheim Ducks in the second round of the 2014 NHL Entry Draft, Montour spent his first two plus NHL seasons in Anaheim before getting traded to the Buffalo Sabres at the 2019 deadline in exchange for defenseman Brendan Guhle and a first-round pick. After just 112 games for Buffalo spread over three seasons, he was traded to the Florida Panthers at the 2021 deadline for a third-round pick. Montour peaked in Florida, having his career-best campaign in 2022-23 with 16 goals and 57 assists for 73 points in 80 games, and helping the Panthers win the Stanley Cup in 2024 before departing for Seattle. After Thursday’s game in Tampa, the Kraken will finish up a five-game road trip against the Panthers on Saturday.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images A journeyman has found a new home in the Lone Star State. The Dallas Stars announced on Friday that they have signed forward David Perron to a one-year contract. The deal carries a prorated cap hit of $850,000 for the 2026-27 season. Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman was the first to report the signing. When the new season began, the 38-year-old remained unsigned . However, in the opening weeks of the campaign, the Stars realized they could utilize the tools the 20-year NHLer possesses. Perron moves to Dallas hoping to produce a little bit more and stay healthier than he has in the past couple of seasons. After an impressive stretch in which he posted at least 45 points eight years in a row, the Stanley Cup champion posted only 16 points in 43 games with the Ottawa Senators in 2024-25, improving only slightly to 28 points in 65 appearances last year. He started last season with the Sens before the trade deadline , when he was traded to the Detroit Red Wings , though he did little to better the Original Six team’s postseason chances, scoring just three goals in 16 contests. The Sherbrooke, Que. native has made his way around the NHL over his long career. After starting off with the St. Louis Blues , the team that took him in the first round of the 2007 NHL Draft, he was traded to the Edmonton Oilers in the summer of 2013. He was then dealt to the Pittsburgh Penguins in the middle of the 20214-15 campaign, but was on the move the following season, as he was traded to the Anaheim Ducks . He rejoined the Blues as a free agent in July 2016, but the Vegas Golden Knights claimed him in the expansion draft a year later. After one season in Sin City, he returned to the Blues and helped the franchise win its first Cup.

Morrissey is the Jets’ clear-cut No. 1 defenseman, a two-way force who shoulders a substantial workload on a nightly basis. The Red Wings entered the season already with the longest active playoff drought, but off-season turmoil on multiple fronts created plenty of noise as the team returned to the ice in September. That turmoil included an unresolved trade request from former captain Dylan Larkin, a prolonged contract negotiation with top-pair defenceman Simon Edvinsson and Ilitch's decision to fire general manager Steve Yzerman in July. Yzerman's replacement has not been found and Shawn Horcoff was promoted to interim general manager in mid-September, tasked with trying to get the team back on track. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Ottawa’s Drake Batherson preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to Stephen Halliday’s goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 8:10 (11:50 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Acquire Aatu Raty By Brennan McClain | at October 15, 2026 5:25 pm A few hours after clearing waivers , center Aatu Räty is granted a new opportunity. According to a team announcement , the Toronto Maple Leafs have acquired Räty from the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for forwards Jacob Quillan and Brandon Buhr . Although the Maple Leafs could have acquired Räty for nothing via waivers, there is a method to the madness. If Toronto claimed him and tried to assign him to the AHL’s Toronto Marlies, they would have to waive him again. However, because the Maple Leafs waited for Räty to clear waivers before acquiring him, he now becomes more flexible. Räty now must play in 10 games or be on the roster for 30 days before being eligible for waivers again. Additionally, Toronto already had the maximum 50 standard contracts in the organization, prohibiting them from placing a claim on Räty. Even if he doesn’t raise his offensive ceiling in Toronto, Räty still has much to offer the Maple Leafs.
